claims.text: The proposed hybrid machine-learning framework combines ab initio defect-scattering features with empirical conductivity measurements.
The model includes features representing scattering associated with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model can accurately predict the temperature-dependent electrical conductivity of polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The hybrid model will outperform traditional analytical conductivity methods that assume ideal, defect-free crystals.
The target material is bulk polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr with typical microstructural defects and approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Quantum effects and defect scattering dominate electrical transport in this material over 0–200 K.
Phonon scattering dominates electrical transport in this material over 300–1200 K.
Oxygen impurities and grain boundaries produce local lattice distortions and defect distributions.
These local distortions and defect distributions mediate electron scattering that perfect-crystal approximations do not capture.
Correlating ab initio features with empirical conductivity data allows the model to learn the interplay between defect-induced and phonon scattering.
Learning non-ideal scattering behavior will correct inaccuracies in traditional analytical conductivity predictions.
For samples containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen, predicted conductivity will be within 10% of measurements throughout both specified temperature regimes.
Existing analytical conductivity approaches typically assume defect-free single crystals.
Existing analytical approaches give inaccurate conductivity predictions for defect-containing HfNbTaTiZr in both specified temperature regimes.
The claimed applicability is limited to polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen at 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Model validity in the 200–300 K interval is uncertain because neither scattering mechanism may dominate independently there.
Model validity is uncertain for oxygen concentrations significantly different from 1 wt.%.
It remains unvalidated whether the ab initio features capture all relevant complexities of a bulk polycrystalline microstructure.
A held-out approximately 1 wt.% oxygen specimen will be benchmarked by measuring and predicting conductivity at 150 K and 600 K.
A prediction error greater than 10% at either 150 K or 600 K is specified to falsify the hypothesis.
